practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Test should focus on a single behavior. EVALUATION: The method has a single 'Act' operation: new Grafo(). DECISION: Only one constructor invocation and no additional Arrange-Act-Assert blocks. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Tests must be independent. EVALUATION: The test uses only local variables and does not reference or modify static/instance state; no ordered naming. DECISION: No shared mutable state or setup/teardown required in this method. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Should cover happy and error scenarios. EVALUATION: Only a single test exists and it exercises the happy path (constructor) with no exception/edge-case tests. DECISION: Class has only one test and no exception assertions or @Test(expected)/assertThrows usage. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Boundary testing applies to inputs with ranges. EVALUATION: The tested behavior is a no-argument constructor with no numeric or ranged inputs shown in the method. DECISION: No obvious boundaries to exercise in this constructor context. VERDICT: not-applicable.

PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Tests should be modular and avoid duplication. EVALUATION: Single short test (local variables, no duplicated setup) and no repeated blocks in this class. DECISION: Because the test is short and self-contained, modularity is acceptable. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Tests should be small and simple. EVALUATION: Method is under 20 lines and contains no loops or conditionals. DECISION: Meets low complexity criteria. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Assertions should verify multiple properties to detect faults. EVALUATION: The test contains no assertions, so it cannot verify properties of the created object. DECISION: Only object construction is performed without property checks. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Avoid @Ignore/@Disabled and commented-out tests. EVALUATION: No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations nor commented-out @Test methods visible. DECISION: Tests are active. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Tests should link to requirements. EVALUATION: Class Javadoc and method Javadoc include 'Requirement: REQ-001' and mention REQ-001 in the method comment. DECISION: Explicit traceability is present. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Look for explicit performance/security tests. EVALUATION: The method uses @Test(timeout = 4000), which is an explicit timing constraint. DECISION: Presence of timeout counts as an explicit performance-related test indicator. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Test names should describe scenario and expected result. EVALUATION: Method name is 'test0', which is generic and doesn't convey intent. DECISION: Generic name -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Auto-generated tests often have verbose metadata and generic names. EVALUATION: The class uses EvoSuite artifacts: @RunWith(EvoRunner.class), EvoRunnerParameters and import of org.evosuite.runtime.EvoAssertions, plus the generic test name 'test0' and scaffolding inheritance. DECISION: Signs of heavy code generation observed. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Tests should show design intent. EVALUATION: The method Javadoc contains a Given-When-Then description, indicating BDD-style intent and thoughtful design. DECISION: Presence of Given-When-Then commentary fulfills the criterion. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Tests should exercise public API and avoid internals. EVALUATION: The test calls only the public Grafo() constructor and does not access private fields or use reflection. DECISION: Interacts with public API only. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Assertions should be specific and include messages. EVALUATION: The test contains no assertions; therefore it cannot fail to detect incorrect behavior. DECISION: Absence of any assertions -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Comments should explain why. EVALUATION: The class and method include concise Javadoc with Given-When-Then and a requirement reference; there is no excessive or commented-out code. DECISION: Comments add value and are minimal. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Tests should avoid nondeterminism. EVALUATION: The test contains no Random, System.currentTimeMillis, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies within the method body. DECISION: Deterministic behavior observed. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Tests should not leave side effects. EVALUATION: The test only constructs an object and uses only local variables; no files, DB writes, or static state modifications are visible. DECISION: No side effects detected. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE/RATIONALE: Tests should use tags/categories to organize. EVALUATION: No @Tag/@Category annotations are present at class or method level. DECISION: Absence of any categorization -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.
